# `silk/core/effect`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Combinators for lazy effect values: transform success, recover typed failures, supply services,
and run cleanup.

## When to use
An `Effect<A ! E ? R>` is a computation that can succeed with `A`, fail with a typed value `E`,
and needs the providers `R`. Use [`map`](#Effect.impl.map) and [`flatMap`](#Effect.impl.flatMap) to continue after success. Use
[`mapError`](#Effect.impl.mapError), [`catch`](#Effect.impl.catch), or [`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll) for typed failures. Use [`provide`](#Effect.impl.provide) or [`provideMut`](#Effect.impl.provideMut)
to supply a service, and [`ensuring`](#Effect.impl.ensuring) for cleanup. For plain sequential code, direct `run`
statements are often clearer than combinators.

## Details
Combinators are lazy. When code passes an effect to a combinator, the effect does not run. Most
combinators take a `once Effect`, so that value runs at most one time. [`retry`](#Effect.impl.retry) takes a
reusable effect because it can run the effect more than one time.

Sequential combinators stop at the first typed failure, unless a recovery operation handles it.
The signatures show how the channels combine. Two steps usually give the unions `! E | F` and
`? R | S`.

A provider operation removes one exact requirement from `R`. If one provider can satisfy more
than one requirement, write the requirement as the first type argument, as in
`Effect.provideMut<Logger at Audit>`. Shared, exclusive, and owned providers have different
borrow and capture rules.

## Gotchas
A typed failure is an outcome that combinators can catch. A trap is not an outcome. A trap
bypasses [`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll), [`ensuring`](#Effect.impl.ensuring), and `Drop` hooks. If the execution stack is exhausted, the
program traps.

## Examples
### Transform and continue a successful computation
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

struct Problem {
  code: i32,
}

effect fn read(value: i32) -> i32
  ! Problem {
  if value < 0 {
    fail Problem { code: -1 }
  }
  return value
}

fn double(value: i32) -> i32 {
  return value * 2
}

effect fn addTwo(value: i32) -> i32
  ! Problem {
  return value + 2
}

effect fn recover(error: Problem) -> i32 {
  return error.code
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let computation = read(20) |> Effect.map(double) |> Effect.flatMap(addTwo)
  let answer = run Effect.catchAll(computation, recover)
  if answer != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Supply a custom service for one computation
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

service Clock {
  effect fn value() -> i32 ? &Clock
}

struct FixedClock {
  value: i32,
}

impl Clock for FixedClock {
  effect fn value(self: &Self) -> i32 {
    return self.value
  }
}

effect fn readClock() -> i32
  ? &Clock {
  return run Clock.value()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let clock = FixedClock { value: 42 }
  let value = run Effect.provide(readClock(), &clock)
  if value != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

### Recover a typed failure into success
```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

struct Problem {
  fallback: i32,
}

effect fn load() -> i32
  ! Problem {
  fail Problem { fallback: 42 }
}

effect fn recover(error: Problem) -> i32 {
  return error.fallback
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let value = run Effect.catchAll(load(), recover)
  if value != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

Import as `Effect` with `import silk.core.effect { Effect }`.

<a id="Effect"></a>

## `Effect`

```silk
pub struct Effect
```

The owner type of the effect combinators. It has no fields and is never constructed.

### Details

`import silk.core.effect { Effect }` gives access to `Effect.map`, `Effect.catchAll`, and the other
combinators. This struct is not the built-in type `Effect<A ! E ? R>`, which needs no import.

<a id="Effect.impl.log"></a>

### Associated function `log`

```silk
pub effect fn log<Args>(
    static template: string<'static>,
    args: &Args
  ) -> () ! LogError ? &mut Logger
```

Sends one log message at `LogLevel.Info` to the active `Logger`.

#### When to use

Use `log` for an ordinary progress message. Use [`logAt`](#Effect.impl.logAt) or a level function, such as
[`logWarning`](#Effect.impl.logWarning), for a different level.

#### Details

`template` is a static format template. The compiler checks it against `args` at compile time.
The `Logger` provider selects the output format and destination. The message is one complete
log event.

#### Errors

- `LogError` if the `Logger` provider fails. This function does not buffer or retry.

<a id="Effect.impl.result"></a>

### Associated function `result`

```silk
pub effect fn result<'env, A, E, ?R>(
    protected: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>
  ) -> Result<A, E> ? R
```

Runs `protected` one time and returns its outcome as a [`Result`](./core-result.md#Result) value.

#### When to use

Use `result` when the caller must keep, inspect, or store a failure as data, instead of
letting it propagate. Use [`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll) when the caller only needs to recover to a success
value.

#### Details

The output effect has no typed failures. A success becomes `Result.Success` and a typed
failure becomes `Result.Failure`. The output effect still needs the providers `R`.

#### Gotchas

A trap is not a typed failure. `result` does not catch a trap.

#### Examples

##### Inspect a failure as a value

```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.core.result { Result }

struct Problem {
  code: i32,
}

effect fn load() -> i32
  ! Problem {
  fail Problem { code: 7 }
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let completed = run Effect.result(load())
  let code = match move completed {
    Result<i32, Problem>.Success { value } => 0
    Result<i32, Problem>.Failure { error } => error.code
  }
  if code != 7 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Effect.impl.mapBoth"></a>

### Method `mapBoth`

```silk
pub effect fn mapBoth<'env, A, B, E, F, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onSuccess: once fn<'env>(A) -> B,
    onFailure: once fn<'env>(E) -> F
  ) -> B ! F ? R
```

Runs `self` and transforms its success with `onSuccess` or its typed failure with `onFailure`.

#### Details

One callback runs, after `self` completes. `onSuccess` changes `A` to `B`. `onFailure` changes
`E` to `F`, and the output effect fails with that `F`. The providers `R` stay required. A trap
bypasses both callbacks.

When diagnostic observation is active, the new failure keeps the original failure as its
cause.

<a id="Effect.impl.map"></a>

### Method `map`

```silk
pub effect fn map<'env, A, B, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onSuccess: once fn<'env>(A) -> B
  ) -> B ! E ? R
```

Runs `self` and returns `onSuccess(value)` for its success value.

#### When to use

Use `map` when the next step is a plain function that cannot fail. Use [`flatMap`](#Effect.impl.flatMap) when the
next step is an effect.

#### Details

`onSuccess` runs one time, after `self` succeeds. If `self` fails, the failure propagates and
`onSuccess` does not run. The failure type and providers do not change.

<a id="Effect.impl.mapError"></a>

### Method `mapError`

```silk
pub effect fn mapError<'env, A, E, F, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onFailure: once fn<'env>(E) -> F
  ) -> A ! F ? R
```

Runs `self` and, if it fails, changes the typed failure with `onFailure`.

#### When to use

Use `mapError` to convert a failure into the failure type of the caller, or to add context to
a failure. The output still fails. Use [`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll) to recover to a success.

#### Details

`onFailure` runs one time, only if `self` fails. Its result is the new failure. A success does
not change. The new failure keeps the original failure as its diagnostic cause.

<a id="Effect.impl.flatMap"></a>

### Method `flatMap`

```silk
pub effect fn flatMap<'env, A, B, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onSuccess: for<use 'call> once fn<'env>(A) -> once Effect<'call & 'env; B ! F ? S>
  ) -> B ! E | F ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and then runs the effect that `onSuccess` returns for the success value.

#### When to use

Use `flatMap` to chain effects in a pipeline. Use direct `run` statements when named
intermediate values make the code clearer.

#### Details

If `self` fails, `onSuccess` does not run. The output has the failures of both steps (`E | F`)
and the providers of both steps (`R | S`). The success of the second effect is the output
success.

The success value stays valid while the second effect runs and while it cleans up, also when
it suspends or is cancelled. The output effect cannot escape the call scope.

<a id="Effect.impl.flatten"></a>

### Method `flatten`

```silk
pub effect fn flatten<'env, A, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; Effect<'static; A ! F ? S> ! E ? R>
  ) -> A ! E | F ? R | S
```

Runs an outer effect and then runs the inner effect that it returns.

#### Details

If the outer effect fails, there is no inner effect and nothing more runs. The output has the
failures and providers of both effects. `Effect.flatten(nested)` has the same behavior as
[`flatMap`](#Effect.impl.flatMap) with a function that returns its argument.

<a id="Effect.impl.zip"></a>

### Method `zip`

```silk
pub effect fn zip<'env, A, B, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    other: once Effect<'env; B ! F ? S>
  ) -> Pair<A, B> ! E | F ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and then `other`, and returns both success values as a [`Pair`](#Pair).

#### Details

The effects run in order, not in parallel. If `self` fails, `other` does not run. The output
has the failures and providers of both effects. Read the values from `Pair.first` and
`Pair.second`.

<a id="Effect.impl.zip3"></a>

### Method `zip3`

```silk
pub effect fn zip3<'env, A, B, C, E, F, G, ?R, ?S, ?T>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    second: once Effect<'env; B ! F ? S>,
    third: once Effect<'env; C ! G ? T>
  ) -> Triple<A, B, C> ! E | F | G ? R | S | T
```

Runs three effects in order and returns the three success values as a [`Triple`](#Triple).

#### Details

The effects run from left to right, not in parallel. If one effect fails, the later effects do
not run. The output has the failures and providers of all three effects.

<a id="Effect.impl.tap"></a>

### Method `tap`

```silk
pub effect fn tap<'env, A, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    callback: for<use 'call> once fn<'env>(A) -> once Effect<'call & 'env; A ! F ? S>
  ) -> A ! E | F ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and then runs the effect that `callback` returns. The success of that effect is
the output success.

#### When to use

Use `tap` to do an effectful action with a value, such as a log message, and then continue
with the value. The callback must return the value again.

#### Details

`callback` receives the success value by move. It must produce a value of the same type `A`.
If `self` fails, `callback` does not run. A failure of either step propagates.

<a id="Effect.impl.catchAll"></a>

### Method `catchAll`

```silk
pub effect fn catchAll<'env, A, B, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onFailure: for<use 'call> once fn<'env>(E) -> once Effect<'call & 'env; B ! F ? S>
  ) -> A | B ! F ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and, if it fails, runs the effect that `onFailure` returns for the failure.

#### When to use

Use `catchAll` to recover from every typed failure of `self`. Use [`catch`](#Effect.impl.catch) to recover from
one failure type and let the other failure types propagate.

#### Details

`onFailure` runs one time, only if `self` fails, and receives the complete failure value. The
output has no failures of `self`. It can fail only with the failures `F` of the recovery
effect. A success of `self` bypasses `onFailure`. The output needs the providers of both
paths.

The failure value stays valid while the recovery effect runs and cleans up, also when it
suspends or is cancelled.

#### Gotchas

A trap is not a typed failure. `catchAll` does not catch a trap.

<a id="Effect.impl.catch"></a>

### Method `catch`

```silk
pub effect fn catch<'env, S, A, B, E, F, ?R, ?Q>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onFailure: for<use 'call> once fn<'env>(S) -> once Effect<'call & 'env; B ! F ? Q>
  ) -> A | B ! Without<E, S> | F ? R | Q
  where S in E
```

Runs `self` and, if it fails with the failure type `S`, runs the effect that `onFailure`
returns.

#### When to use

Use `catch` to recover from one failure type and let the other failures propagate. Use
[`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll) to recover from each failure.

#### Details

Write the selected type as the first type argument, as in `Effect.catch<NotFound>(load(),
handler)`. `S` must be one member of the failure union `E`. `onFailure` runs one time, only
for a failure of type `S`. Other failures propagate unchanged, as `Without<E, S>`. The
failures `F` of the recovery effect join the output. A success bypasses `onFailure`.

#### Gotchas

A trap is not a typed failure. `catch` does not catch a trap.

<a id="Effect.impl.ensuring"></a>

### Method `ensuring`

```silk
pub effect fn ensuring<'env, A, E, ?R, ?S>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    finalizer: once Effect<'env; () ! never ? S>
  ) -> A ! E ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and then runs `finalizer`, for a success and for a typed failure. The outcome of
`self` does not change.

#### When to use

Use `ensuring` to release a resource or to record the end of an operation, whatever the
outcome. Use [`ensuringNonParking`](#Effect.impl.ensuringNonParking) when cancellation must also run the finalizer.

#### Details

The order is:

1. `self` runs and cleans up its own local values.
2. `finalizer` runs.
3. The caller receives the success value or the typed failure.

A caller that recovers the failure does not see it before the finalizer completes. The failure
keeps its original origin and context. Both effects can suspend. If a suspended composition is
destroyed, it drops the held outcome one time and does not run the rest of the finalizer.

#### Gotchas

`finalizer` cannot fail (`! never`). To use a cleanup step that can fail, recover its failure
first, for example with [`catchAll`](#Effect.impl.catchAll). A trap bypasses the finalizer.

<a id="Effect.impl.ensuringNonParking"></a>

### Method `ensuringNonParking`

```silk
pub effect fn ensuringNonParking<
    'env,
    A,
    E,
    ?R,
    ?S,
    F: once Effect<'env; () ! never ? S> + Intrinsic.NonParking,
  >(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    finalizer: F
  ) -> A ! E ? R | S
```

Runs `self` and then runs `finalizer` on each exit: success, typed failure, and cancellation.
The outcome of `self` does not change.

#### When to use

Use this function when cancellation of a parked execution must release a scoped resource. Use
[`ensuring`](#Effect.impl.ensuring) when the finalizer must suspend.

#### Details

The finalizer runs one time after success or typed failure, and also when an owner cancels a
parked `Execution`. The providers stay valid until the finalizer completes. Nested finalizers
run in reverse order.

#### Gotchas

`finalizer` must be `Intrinsic.NonParking`, so it cannot suspend. It cannot fail (`! never`).
A trap bypasses the finalizer and all `Drop` hooks.

<a id="Effect.impl.useReleaseNonParking"></a>

### Associated function `useReleaseNonParking`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn useReleaseNonParking<
    'env,
    Resource: 'env,
    A,
    E,
    ?R,
    ?S,
    Release: for<'scope> once fn<'env>(
      &'scope mut Resource
    ) -> once Effect<'scope & 'env; () ! never ? S> + Intrinsic.NonParking,
  >(
    resource: Resource,
    use: for<'scope> once fn<'env>(
      &'scope mut Resource
    ) -> once Effect<'scope & 'env; A ! E ? R>,
    release: Release
  ) -> A ! E ? R | S
```

Gives an exclusive borrow of `resource` to `use`, and then gives a new exclusive borrow to
`release` on each exit: success, typed failure, and cancellation.

#### When to use

Use this function when work that can suspend needs exclusive access to a resource, and
cancellation must release the resource before the frame is destroyed.

#### Details

The borrow for `use` ends before `release` starts. `release` runs one time. Nested calls
release in reverse order. The outcome of `use` does not change.

#### Gotchas

The effect that `release` returns must be `Intrinsic.NonParking` and cannot fail (`! never`).
Recover a cleanup failure before you return the effect. A trap bypasses `release` and all
`Drop` hooks.

<a id="Effect.impl.ifThenElse"></a>

### Associated function `ifThenElse`

```silk
pub effect fn ifThenElse<'env, A, E, F, ?R, ?S>(
    condition: bool,
    onTrue: once fn<'env>() -> Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    onFalse: once fn<'env>() -> Effect<'env; A ! F ? S>
  ) -> A ! E | F ? R | S
```

Runs the effect of `onTrue` if `condition` is `true`, or the effect of `onFalse` if it is
`false`.

#### When to use

Use `ifThenElse` to select one of two effects in a pipeline. Use an `if` statement with `run`
in plain sequential code.

#### Details

Each branch is a function that makes its effect. Only the selected function runs, so the other
effect is never made. Code that is valid only under the condition is safe in its branch. The
output has the failures and providers of both branches. Both branches must have the same
success type.

The name is not `if` because `if` is a keyword.

<a id="Effect.impl.retry"></a>

### Method `retry`

```silk
pub effect fn retry<'env, A, E, ?R>(
    mut self: mut Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    retries: usize
  ) -> A ! E ? R
```

Runs `self` and, after each typed failure, runs it again, at most `retries` more times.

#### Details

A success stops the attempts. If each attempt fails, the last failure propagates. Earlier
failure values are dropped. A `retries` of 0 gives one attempt. `self` must be a reusable
effect (`mut Effect`).

#### Gotchas

There is no delay between attempts. A trap stops the attempts at once and is not retried.

<a id="Effect.impl.bindRequirement"></a>

### Method `bindRequirement`

```silk
pub effect fn bindRequirement<'env, ?S, A, P, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    provider: &'env P
  ) -> A ! E ? Without<R, S>
  where &'env P provides S from R
```

Satisfies one shared requirement of `self` with a shared borrow of `provider`.

#### When to use

Use [`provide`](#Effect.impl.provide), which has the same behavior. This name shows the relation to
[`bindRequirementMut`](#Effect.impl.bindRequirementMut) and [`bindRequirementOwned`](#Effect.impl.bindRequirementOwned).

#### Details

Write the selected requirement as the first type argument when the selection is not unique. A
shared provider can satisfy only a shared requirement. The output does not need that
requirement. The borrow ends when the effect completes, and the caller keeps ownership of
`provider`.

<a id="Effect.impl.bindRequirementMut"></a>

### Method `bindRequirementMut`

```silk
pub effect fn bindRequirementMut<'env, ?S, A, P, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    provider: &'env mut P
  ) -> A ! E ? Without<R, S>
  where &'env mut P provides S from R
```

Satisfies one requirement of `self` with an exclusive borrow of `provider`.

#### When to use

Use [`provideMut`](#Effect.impl.provideMut) in ordinary code. It has the same behavior.

#### Details

An exclusive provider can satisfy a shared or an exclusive requirement. The output does not
need the exact requirement that was selected. For example, `&mut P` for a shared `&Logger`
removes `&Logger`. The caller gets exclusive access back when the effect completes.

<a id="Effect.impl.bindRequirementOwned"></a>

### Method `bindRequirementOwned`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn bindRequirementOwned<'env, ?S, A, P: 'env, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    provider: P
  ) -> A ! E ? Without<R, S>
  where P provides S from R
```

Satisfies one requirement of `self` with `provider`, which moves into the output effect.

#### When to use

Use this function when the provider must live as long as the effect, for example when the
caller returns the effect.

#### Details

An owned provider can satisfy a shared or an exclusive requirement. If `provider` is affine,
the output effect can run one time. If `provider` is `Copy`, the effect keeps a copy and can
run again. The provider is dropped with the effect. It is not returned.

<a id="Effect.impl.provide"></a>

### Method `provide`

```silk
pub effect fn provide<'env, ?S, A, P, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    provider: &'env P
  ) -> A ! E ? Without<R, S>
  where &'env P provides S from R
```

Satisfies one shared requirement of `self` with a shared borrow of `provider`.

#### When to use

Use `provide` for a service that the computation only reads, such as a clock or a
configuration. Use [`provideMut`](#Effect.impl.provideMut) when the service changes state.

#### Details

The output does not need the selected requirement. Each other requirement stays in the output
type. The caller keeps ownership of `provider`. This function has the same behavior as
[`bindRequirement`](#Effect.impl.bindRequirement).

#### Gotchas

If `provider` can satisfy more than one requirement, write the requirement as the first type
argument, as in `Effect.provide<Clock>(...)`.

<a id="Effect.impl.provideMut"></a>

### Method `provideMut`

```silk
pub effect fn provideMut<'env, ?S, A, P, E, ?R>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    provider: &'env mut P
  ) -> A ! E ? Without<R, S>
  where &'env mut P provides S from R
```

Satisfies one requirement of `self` with an exclusive borrow of `provider`.

#### When to use

Use `provideMut` for a service that changes state, such as an allocator, a logger, or a
counter. Use [`provide`](#Effect.impl.provide) for a read-only service.

#### Details

The compiler selects the requirement by provider identity or by one unique service
conformance. The order of requirements in the type is never used for selection. The output
does not need the selected requirement. `provider` does not move, and the caller gets
exclusive access back when the effect completes.

#### Gotchas

If `provider` can satisfy more than one requirement, write the requirement as the first type
argument, as in `Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(...)`.

#### Examples

##### Change a custom service in one computation

```silk
import silk.core.effect { Effect }

service Counter {
  effect fn next() -> i32 ? &mut Counter
}

struct Counting {
  value: i32,
}

effect fn next(self: &mut Counting) -> i32 {
  self.value = self.value + 1
  return self.value
}

impl Counter for Counting {
  next: Counting.next
}

effect fn read() -> i32
  ? &mut Counter {
  return run Counter.next()
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut counter = Counting { value: 41 }
  let value = run Effect.provideMut<Counter>(read(), &mut counter)
  if value != 42 || counter.value != 42 {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}
```

<a id="Effect.impl.provideEffect"></a>

### Method `provideEffect`

```silk
pub effect fn provideEffect<'env, ?S, A, P, E, F, ?R, ?Q>(
    self: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>,
    acquire: Effect<'env; P ! F ? Q>
  ) -> A ! E | F ? Without<R, S> | Q
  where &'env mut P provides S from R
```

Runs `acquire` to make a provider, and then runs `self` with an exclusive borrow of that
provider.

#### When to use

Use `provideEffect` when the provider itself must be made by an effect, such as a connection
that needs an allocator.

#### Details

`acquire` runs each time the output effect runs. Thus a [`retry`](#Effect.impl.retry) of the output makes a new
provider for each attempt. The provider is dropped before the caller sees the outcome of
`self`. The output needs the providers `Q` of `acquire`, and each requirement of `self` except
the selected one.

#### Errors

- `F` if `acquire` fails. Then `self` does not run.
- `E` if `self` fails.

<a id="Effect.impl.suspend"></a>

### Associated function `suspend`

```silk
pub effect fn suspend<'env, A, E, ?R>(
    deferred: once Effect<'env; A ! E ? R>
  ) -> A ! E ? R
```

Runs `deferred` through the stack-safe effect executor. The channels do not change.

#### When to use

Use `suspend` at a recursive or deeply chained boundary, so that deep recursion does not use
the native call stack. Laziness alone does not need `suspend`.

#### Details

`suspend` adds no allocator requirement and no allocation failure. The frames are on the
execution stack of the compiler.

#### Gotchas

If the execution stack is exhausted, the program traps.

<a id="Effect.impl.of"></a>

### Associated function `of`

```silk
pub effect<'env> fn of<A: 'env, 'env>(value: A) -> A
```

Returns an effect that succeeds with `value` when it runs.

#### Details

The call evaluates `value` immediately and moves it into the effect. The effect has no
failures and needs no providers. If `value` is affine, the effect can run one time.

<a id="Effect.impl.sleep"></a>

### Associated function `sleep`

```silk
pub effect fn sleep(howLong: u64) -> () ? &mut MonotonicClock
```

Waits `howLong` nanoseconds on the timeline of the active `MonotonicClock` provider.

#### Details

The provider decides how to wait. A native provider blocks the thread. A test provider can
advance virtual time.

#### Gotchas

A duration of 0 returns without a wait. If the deadline is more than the clock can represent,
the program traps.
